readings.title: Ezekiel Appointed as a Watchman
readings.subtitle: The responsibility to warn the righteous and the wicked.
readings.text: [16] And it came to be at the end of seven days that the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to me, saying, [17] <dq>“Son of man, <dn>I</dn> have made <dn>את</dn> you a watchman for the house of Yisra’ěl. And you shall hear a word from <dn>My</dn> mouth, and shall warn them from <dn>Me</dn>.</dq> [18] <dq>“When <dn>I</dn> say to the wrong, ‘You shall certainly die,’ and you have not warned him, nor spoken to warn the wrong from his wrong way, to save his life, that same wrong man shall die in his crookedness, and <dn>את</dn> his blood <dn>I</dn> require at your hand.</dq> [19] <dq>“But if you have warned the wrong and he does not turn from his wrong, nor from his wrong way, he shall die in his crookedness, and you have delivered your being.</dq> [20] <dq>“And when a righteous one turns from his righteousness and shall do unrighteousness, when <dn>I</dn> have put a stumbling-block before him, he shall die. Because you did not warn him, he shall die in his sin, and his righteousness which he has done is not remembered, and <dn>את</dn> his blood <dn>I</dn> require at your hand.</dq> [21] <dq>“But if you have warned the righteous one that the righteous should not sin, and he did not sin, he shall certainly live because he has been warned, and you have delivered your being.”</dq>

readings.title: Ezekiel Struck Dumb
readings.subtitle: He is confined to his house and his tongue is bound until YeHoVaH speaks.
readings.text: [22] And the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came upon me there, and <dn>He</dn> said to me, <dq>“Arise, go out into the plain, so that <dn>I</dn> might speak to you there.”</dq> [23] So I got up and went out into the plain, and see, the esteem of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> stood there, like the esteem which I saw by the River Keḇar, and I fell on my face. [24] And the Spirit entered me and set me on my feet, and spoke with me and said to me, <dq>“Go, shut yourself inside your house.</dq> [25] <dq>“And you, O son of man, see, they shall put cords on you and bind you with them, so that you do not go out in their midst.</dq> [26] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> make your tongue stick to the roof of your mouth, so that you shall be dumb and not be a reprover to them, for they are a rebellious house.</dq> [27] <dq>“But when <dn>I</dn> speak with you, <dn>I</dn> open your mouth, and you shall say to them, ‘Thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’ <dn>He</dn> who hears, let him hear. And he who refuses, let him refuse, for they are a rebellious house.</dq>

readings.title: The Siege Portrayed
readings.subtitle: Ezekiel enacts the siege of Jerusalem on a clay tablet and lies on his side for the years of iniquity.
readings.text: [1] <dq>“And you, son of man, take <dn>את</dn> a clay tablet, and you shall lay it before you, and shall inscribe on it <dn>את</dn> a city, <dn>את</dn> Yerushalayim,</dq> [2] <dq>and shall lay siege against it, and build a siege wall against it, and heap up a mound against it, and set camps against it, and place battering rams against it all around.</dq> [3] <dq>“Then take <dn>את</dn> an iron plate, and set it as an iron wall between you and the city. And you shall set your face against it, and it shall be besieged, and you shall lay siege against it. It is a sign to the house of Yisra’ěl.</dq> [4] <dq>“And lie on your left side, and you shall put <dn>את</dn> the crookedness of the house of Yisra’ěl on it. As many days as you lie on it, you shall bear their crookedness.</dq> [5] <dq>“For <dn>I</dn> <dn>Myself</dn> have laid on you the years of their crookedness, according to the number of the days, three hundred and ninety days. And you shall bear <dn>את</dn> the crookedness of the house of Yisra’ěl.</dq> [6] <dq>“And when you have completed them, you shall lie again on your right side and shall bear <dn>את</dn> the crookedness of the house of Yehuḏah forty days, a day for a year. <dn>I</dn> have laid on you a day for a year.</dq> [7] <dq>“Then you shall set your face toward the siege of Yerushalayim, with your arm bared, and you shall prophesy against it.</dq> [8] <dq>“And see, <dn>I</dn> shall put cords on you so that you do not turn from one side to another until you have completed the days of your siege.</dq>

readings.title: The Bread of Defilement
readings.subtitle: Ezekiel is commanded to eat rationed and defiled bread as a sign of the coming famine and exile.
readings.text: [9] <dq>“And take <dn>את</dn> wheat, and <dn>את</dn> barley, and beans, and lentils, and millet, and spelt. And you shall put them into one vessel, and make bread of them. You shall eat it, as many days as you lie on your side, three hundred and ninety days.</dq> [10] <dq>“And your food which you eat is by weight, twenty sheqels a day, to be eaten from time to time.</dq> [11] <dq>“And drink water by measure, one-sixth of a hin, to be drunk from time to time.</dq> [12] <dq>“And eat it as a barley cake. And bake it, before their eyes, on human dung.”</dq> [13] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>“Even so the children of Yisra’ěl shall eat their defiled bread among the nations, to whom <dn>I</dn> drive them.”</dq> [14] Then I said, “Ah, Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>! See, I have never defiled myself from my youth till now. I have never eaten what died of itself or was torn by beasts, nor has unclean meat ever come into my mouth.” [15] And <dn>He</dn> said to me, <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am giving you the dung of cattle instead of human dung, and you shall prepare your bread over it.”</dq> [16] And <dn>He</dn> said to me, <dq>“Son of man, see, <dn>I</dn> am going to cut off <dn>את</dn> the supply of bread in Yerushalayim, and they shall eat bread by weight and with fear, and drink water by measure and with dread,</dq> [17] <dq>so that they lack bread and water, and shall be appalled with one another, and be consumed in their crookedness.</dq>

readings.title: The Command to Wear Yokes
readings.subtitle: Jeremiah is instructed to make yokes and send them to the surrounding kings as a sign of submission to Nebuchadnezzar.
readings.text: [1] In the beginning of the reign of Yehoyaqim son of Yoshiyahu, the sovereign of Yehuḏah, this word came to Yirmeyah from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, [2] <dq>“This is what <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to me, ‘Make for yourselves bands and yokes. Then you shall put them on your neck,</dq> [3] <dq>and shall send them to the sovereign of Eḏom, and the sovereign of Mo’aḇ, and the sovereign of the Ammonites, and the sovereign of Tsor, and the sovereign of Tsiḏon, by the hand of the messengers who come to Yerushalayim to Tsiḏqiyahu, the sovereign of Yehuḏah.</dq> [4] <dq>And you shall command them to say to their masters, “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, ‘Say this to your masters,’</dq> [5] <dq><dn>I</dn> have made <dn>את</dn> the earth, <dn>את</dn> the man and <dn>את</dn> the beast that are on the face of the earth, by <dn>My</dn> great power and by <dn>My</dn> outstretched arm. And <dn>I</dn> shall give it to whom it seemed right in <dn>My</dn> eyes.</dq> [6] <dq>And now, <dn>I</dn> have given <dn>את</dn> all these lands into the hand of Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar the sovereign of Baḇel, <dn>My</dn> servant. And <dn>את</dn> the beasts of the field <dn>I</dn> have also given him to serve him.</dq> [7] <dq>And all nations shall serve him and his son and his son’s son, until the time of his land comes. And then many nations and great sovereigns shall make him serve them.</dq> [8] <dq>And it shall be, <dn>את</dn> the nation and <dn>את</dn> the reign that do not serve Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar the sovereign of Baḇel, and <dn>את</dn> the one that does not put <dn>את</dn> its neck under the yoke of the sovereign of Baḇel, <dn>את</dn> that nation <dn>I</dn> shall punish,’ declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, ‘with the sword, and the scarcity of food, and the pestilence, until <dn>I</dn> have consumed them by his hand.</dq> [9] <dq>So do not listen to your prophets, or to your diviners, or to your dreamers, or to your observers of clouds, or your sorcerers, who speak to you, saying, “Do not serve the sovereign of Baḇel.”</dq> [10] <dq>For they are prophesying falsehood to you, to remove you far from your land. And <dn>I</dn> shall drive you out, and you shall perish.</dq> [11] <dq>But the nations that bring their necks under the yoke of the sovereign of Baḇel and serve him, <dn>I</dn> shall leave in their own land,’ declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, ’and they shall till it and dwell in it.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: A Warning to Zedekiah
readings.subtitle: Jeremiah urges the king, priests, and people of Judah to submit to Babylon and not listen to false prophets.
readings.text: [12] And I spoke to Tsiḏqiyah the sovereign of Yehuḏah according to all these words, saying, “Bring your necks under the yoke of the sovereign of Baḇel, and serve him and his people, and live! [13] “Why should you die, you and your people, by the sword, by the scarcity of food, and by the pestilence, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken against the nation that does not serve the sovereign of Baḇel? [14] “Do not listen to the words of the prophets who speak to you, saying, ‘Do not serve the sovereign of Baḇel,’ for they prophesy falsehood to you, [15] <dq>for <dn>I</dn> have not sent them,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“yet they prophesy falsehood in <dn>My</dn> Name, in order that <dn>I</dn> drive you out. Then you shall perish, you and the prophets who prophesy to you.”</dq> [16] Then I spoke to the priests and to all this people, saying, “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘Do not listen to the words of your prophets who are prophesying to you, saying, “See, the vessels of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> are brought back from Baḇel soon now,” for they prophesy falsehood to you.</dq> [17] <dq>Do not listen to them. Serve the sovereign of Baḇel, and live! Why should this city become a ruin?</dq> [18] <dq>But if they are prophets, and if the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is with them, let them now make intercession to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, that the vessels which are left in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and in the house of the sovereign of Yehuḏah, and at Yerushalayim, shall not go to Baḇel.’</dq> [19] <dq>“For thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts concerning the columns, and concerning the Sea, and concerning the stands, and concerning the remainder of the vessels which are left in this city,</dq> [20] <dq>which Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar the sovereign of Baḇel did not take, when he exiled Yeḵonyah the son of Yehoyaqim, the sovereign of Yehuḏah, from Yerushalayim to Baḇel, and all the nobles of Yehuḏah and Yerushalayim –</dq> [21] <dq>thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, concerning the vessels that remain in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and in the house of the sovereign of Yehuḏah and of Yerushalayim:</dq> [22] <dq>They shall be brought to Baḇel, and be there until the day that <dn>I</dn> visit them,’</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dq>‘Then <dn>I</dn> shall bring them back and restore them to this place.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: Hananiah's False Prophecy
readings.subtitle: The prophet Hananiah breaks Jeremiah's yoke and falsely prophesies a swift return from exile.
readings.text: [1] And it came to be in that year, at the beginning of the reign of Tsiḏqiyah sovereign of Yehuḏah, in the fourth year and in the fifth new moon, that Ḥananyah son of Azzur the prophet, who was from Giḇ‛on, spoke to me in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> in the presence of the priests and of all the people, saying, [2] “Thus spoke <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, saying, ‘<dn>I</dn> have broken <dn>את</dn> the yoke of the sovereign of Baḇel. [3] Within two years <dn>I</dn> am going to bring back to this place <dn>את</dn> all the vessels of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, that Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar sovereign of Baḇel removed from this place and took to Baḇel. [4] And <dn>I</dn> am going to bring back to this place <dn>את</dn> Yeḵonyah son of Yehoyaqim, sovereign of Yehuḏah, with all the exiles of Yehuḏah who went to Baḇel,’ declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, ‘for <dn>I</dn> am going to break <dn>את</dn> the yoke of the sovereign of Baḇel.’ ” [5] Then the prophet Yirmeyah spoke to the prophet Ḥananyah in the presence of the priests and in the presence of all the people who stood in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, [6] and the prophet Yirmeyah said, “Aměn! <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> do so! <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> establish your words which you have prophesied, to bring back the vessels of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and all the exiles from Baḇel to this place! [7] “Only, hear now this word that I speak in your hearing and in the hearing of all the people: [8] “The prophets who have been before me and before you of old prophesied against many lands and great reigns, of battle and of evil and of pestilence. [9] “The prophet who prophesies of peace – when the word of the prophet comes to pass, that prophet is known as one whom <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has truly sent.” [10] And Ḥananyah the prophet took <dn>את</dn> the yoke off the prophet Yirmeyah’s neck and broke it. [11] And Ḥananyah spoke in the presence of all the people, saying, “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, ‘So <dn>I</dn> shall break <dn>את</dn> the yoke of Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar sovereign of Baḇel from the neck of all nations within two years.’ ” And the prophet Yirmeyah went his way.

readings.title: The Yoke of Iron
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH declares that a yoke of iron will replace the broken wooden yoke, and pronounces death upon Hananiah.
readings.text: [12] And the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to Yirmeyah, after Ḥananyah the prophet had broken the yoke from the neck of the prophet Yirmeyah, saying, [13] <dq>“Go and speak to Ḥananyah, saying, ‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “You have broken the yokes of wood, but you shall make yokes of iron instead.”</dq> [14] <dq>For thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, “<dn>I</dn> have put a yoke of iron on the neck of all these nations, to serve Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar sovereign of Baḇel. And they shall serve him. And <dn>I</dn> have also given him the beasts of the field.” ’ ”</dq> [15] And the prophet Yirmeyah said to Ḥananyah the prophet, “Listen, please, Ḥananyah, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has not sent you, but you have made this people trust in falsehood. [16] “Therefore thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘See, <dn>I</dn> am sending you away from the face of the earth. This year you shall die, for you have spoken apostasy against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’ ”</dq> [17] And Ḥananyah the prophet died the same year, in the seventh new moon.

readings.title: A Message to Babylon
readings.subtitle: Jeremiah commands Seraiah to read a prophecy against Babylon and then sink the scroll in the Euphrates as a sign of its permanent fall.
readings.text: [59] The <dn>את</dn> word that Yirmeyahu the prophet commanded Serayah son of Něriyah, son of Maḥsěyah, when he went with Tsiḏqiyahu the sovereign of Yehuḏah to Baḇel in the fourth year of his reign. And Serayah was a quartermaster. [60] So Yirmeyahu wrote in a book <dn>את</dn> all the evil that would come upon Baḇel, all these words which have been written concerning Baḇel. [61] And Yirmeyahu said to Serayah, “When you come to Baḇel and see it, and read <dn>את</dn> all these words, [62] then you shall say, ‘O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, You have spoken concerning this place to cut <dn>את</dn> it off, so that none shall dwell in it, neither man nor beast, for it is a ruin forever.’ [63] “And it shall be, when you have ended reading this book, that you shall tie a stone to <dn>את</dn> it and throw <dn>את</dn> it into the midst of the Euphrates, [64] and shall say, ‘So does Baḇel sink and not rise from the evil that <dn>I</dn> am bringing upon her, and they shall weary themselves.’ ” Thus far are the words of Yirmeyahu.
